question: Walk me through what I have to do today
subtitle: The four open decisions, in the order that avoids re-work

prose: You have four decisions waiting and one of them closes at 17:00. Two of the four sit on the same supplier, so the order matters — taken in the order below, nothing has to be decided twice.

steps.title: NPI-0417 · Dual-source the aseptic fill-finish slot
steps.body: Vetter Ravensburg cancelled the 12 Oct fill slot. Sourcing priced three alternatives; Siegfried recovers 38 of the 47 days for €340k. G3 moves 04 Nov → 21 Dec if you do nothing.

steps.title: NPI-0402 · Release 2,600 units at risk
steps.body: Tooling is booked from 02 Nov and the slot lapses if the build is not released. Finance modelled three volumes: 2,600 units caps exposure at €1.7M, above your €1.5M authority.

steps.title: NPI-0388 · Activate the Aptar second source before G2
steps.body: Same supplier as 0417. Decide 0417 first — if line 3 stops, the second source stops being a choice and becomes the plan. 19 days of float left.

steps.title: NPI-0371 · Sign the two G2 target product profile
steps.body: Human factors and transit summaries. Quality drafted both from the test data, traced, no criteria waived. G2 closes on schedule if you sign.

why: They are the same supplier: Aptar. Deciding 0417 first removes one option from 0388
0402 and 0371 are independent — take them in any order before their dates
Nothing else needs you this week. 95 of the 107 activities run without asking you
answer.confidence: These four are every open item where the next step is yours. Four more are moving without you.

evidence.label: The Launch Board

evidence.label: K. Tanaka · R&D

answer.rec: Only NPI-0365 needs a push from you
why: The response pack has been drafted and unsigned for 6 days, and every one of those days is a day of G4
The other three have a dated next step inside this week
An escalation travels upwards only — you cannot pull 0365 back and sign it yourself
answer.confidence: Read from the ownership field on every open record, not from a status someone typed.

question: Diagnose the Berobenatide OB launch
subtitle: P3, G3 on 04 Nov, and the one cause behind four findings

prose: Berobenatide OB is in P3 — process validation and supplier qualification, with G3 Submission Commit on 04 Nov 2026. The design work is not the problem. Both live threats are supplier threats, and both are the same supplier.

evidence.label: Gate at risk
evidence.value: G3 Submission Commit · 04 Nov 2026 · would move to 21 Dec

evidence.label: Revenue exposed
evidence.value: €18.4M on the G3 slip, €6.2M on the G2 design freeze

evidence.label: Open findings
evidence.value: 4 — two are yours to decide, two the fleet is still working

evidence.label: Common cause
evidence.value: Aptar. Single source on the frozen BOM, downgraded to High financial risk

evidence.label: Lead market
evidence.value: Germany, then France and Spain · CHMP Q4 review slot holds for now

answer.rec: Treat this as one supplier decision, not four findings
why: NPI-0417 (fill-finish slot) and NPI-0412 (line 3 out of spec) are both Aptar-driven; NPI-0388 is the Aptar credit downgrade itself
Activating the qualified second source at Neuss answers all three at once, and it is cheapest before the G2 freeze on 30 Sep
After G2 the same change costs 11 weeks of change control
answer.confidence: High confidence · the BOM trace, the credit file and the SPC data all point at one part.

question: What is putting the G3 gate at risk?
subtitle: The single cancelled slot behind a 47-day slip

prose: One thing: the 12 Oct fill-finish line slot at Vetter Ravensburg, cancelled by the supplier. Without it the PPQ validation report slips to 19 Dec, MAA (EMA) section 4.3 stays open, and the CHMP Q4 review slot lapses — another 31 days on top of the 47.
prose2: The fleet has already done the work. Quality read the cancellation off the portal, Planning recomputed the critical path, Sourcing priced three alternative sites and Regulatory checked the dossier would survive a 9-day shift. What is left is a €340k authorisation, which is yours.

evidence.label: As planned
evidence.value: G3 Submission Commit · 04 Nov 2026

evidence.label: If nothing changes
evidence.value: 21 Dec 2026 · +47 days

evidence.label: With Siegfried
evidence.value: 13 Nov 2026 · +9 days, for €340k

evidence.label: Checked against
evidence.value: CHMP Q4 slot holds at +9 days. It does not hold at +47.

why: Recovers 38 of the 47 days — the only option of the three that keeps the CHMP slot
Switching modality to X-ray costs 62 days and €1.1M and forfeits the slot
Going US-first needs a G1 reversal, which is a bigger decision than this one
answer.confidence: High confidence · based on 6 comparable fill-finish requalifications across Biopharma.

question: Trace the Aptar line 3 failure agent by agent
subtitle: Line monitor → Quality → Sourcing → Planning → you

prose: This one arrived two minutes ago and has already crossed four agents. It is the clearest example of the handoff in the fleet: a line monitor finds a physical drift, and it ends as a gate decision on your desk.

steps.title: Line Monitor agent — flagged the dimensional drift
steps.body: SPC rule 2 broken on 4 consecutive lots on the lyophilisation stopper dimensional check. Raised without anyone asking it to look.

steps.title: Quality agent — pulled and re-measured all 12 lots
steps.body: 4 confirmed out of tolerance. Scope established: it is 4 lots, not the whole line.

steps.title: Sourcing agent — checked the qualified alternatives
steps.body: 2 approved sites, 1 with capacity now. Neuss can take the volume.

steps.title: Planning agent — re-baselined the affected gates
steps.body: G3 holds if the line stops inside 5 days. Beyond that it does not.

steps.title: It is yours — stop line 3 at Aptar?
steps.body: Quarantine the 4 lots and switch to Neuss. Hits Berobenatide OB, Berobenatide T2D and Sigvotatug in Germany, France and Spain.

answer.rec: Stop the line and switch to Neuss
why: The 5-day window is what makes this cheap. Inside it, G3 does not move at all
Three launches share the part, so a wrong call here is a wrong call three times
The fleet cannot stop a supplier line on its own — that guardrail is deliberate
answer.confidence: Four agents, four minutes, no human in the loop until the decision that needed one.

actions.label: See it live on the board

evidence.label: Berobenatide OA · Iberia

Anything without both of those is routed to a person instead, which is why four things are waiting for you and this one is not
Every step is logged. You can reopen it and take the decision yourself

question: Which launches are exposed in Germany?
subtitle: Five launches, one shared constraint, and it is not regulatory

prose: Germany is the lead market for five of the nine launches and it carries the most exposure of any market, because the MAA (EMA) path and the CHMP review slot both sit behind it.

evidence.label: Berobenatide OB
evidence.value: G3 Submission Commit · €18.4M exposed on the fill-finish slot. The CHMP Q4 slot is the constraint, not the validation work.

evidence.label: Berobenatide T2D
evidence.value: G2 CMC Lock 30 Sep · two unsigned target product profile and the Aptar single source. Both are yours this week.

evidence.label: Sigvotatug
evidence.value: G5 First Ship 26 Sep · 340 of 520 launch stock units still uncertified. 3PL fill-finish is running 6 days over plan.

evidence.label: PF-08634404
evidence.value: Transit packaging failed cold-chain transit protocol Sequence D. Re-test 14 Sep.

evidence.label: Berobenatide OA
evidence.value: First ship Q2 2027, same quarter as Berobenatide OB. 14 of 22 German reps are dual-certified, which is the real constraint.

answer.rec: The German constraint is field force, not regulatory
why: Four of the five clear their regulatory path on current dates
Two launches want the same 22 German reps in the same quarter, and only 14 are dual-certified
Moving Berobenatide OA first ship to Q3 2027 uses its float; Berobenatide OB has none
answer.confidence: Medium-high · certification throughput is modelled from the last 6 EP launches.

question: What do the regulators need from us right now?
subtitle: Two open agency clocks, one review slot, and the site visit to prepare

prose: Three agency threads are live across the portfolio, and only one of them is something you can act on. The other two are clocks running on an authority — the honest answer is that acting faster does not move them, so the job is to keep them un-blocked and be ready when they respond.

evidence.label: FDA · Berobenatide OB
evidence.value: NPI-0420 — BLA under review, a deficiency letter is open. 45 days at stake, no approval until the agency responds. This is on the authority, not on us: acting here will not move the date.

evidence.label: CHMP CHMP rapporteur · Berobenatide OB
evidence.value: Q4 review slot holds only while G3 stays at +9 days. Miss the window and the next confirmed slot is February — another 31 days. The slot is the real regulatory deadline, not the validation work.

evidence.label: CHMP CHMP rapporteur · Berobenatide OSA
evidence.value: NPI-0365 — a query-cycle-2 response has been drafted and unsigned for 6 days. The 21-day clock-stop is running. This is the one thread you can move: it needs a qualified signatory, S. Lindqvist, and it is already escalated.

evidence.label: Questions on the table
evidence.value: FDA: fill-finish-residual limits and the extractables and leachables bridge. EMA/CHMP: the comparability rationale. Every query has a traced response pack assembled from the CSR and the Master Batch Record.

evidence.label: On-site audit
evidence.value: CHMP unannounced site visit expected this quarter — a gemba walk of Aptar line 3 and the Neuss second source. The line-3 CAPA and the dimensional SPC record are what they will ask to see.

answer.rec: Push NPI-0365 to signature today; keep FDA and the CHMP slot un-blocked, don't chase them
why: NPI-0365 is the only agency thread where the next step is yours — every unsigned day is a day of G4
The FDA deficiency clock (NPI-0420) is on the authority; acting here won't move it, so the workspace is view-only by design
The CHMP Q4 slot survives at +9 days and lapses at +47 — protecting the G3 date is what protects the review window
answer.confidence: Read from the ownership field on each agency thread, not a status someone typed. Two are authority-bound; one is yours.

question: What is putting Berobenatide OB's commercial batches at risk?
subtitle: Two lines, three batches out of spec, and an overdue CAPA

prose: Manufacturing, not supply. Berobenatide OB runs commercial output on two lines — line 3 and line 5 — and line 3 has produced 3 batches out of spec on the dimensional check. Line 5 is clean and is holding commercial supply for now.
prose2: The reason line 3 is not simply back yet is a CAPA that is overdue: the DMAIC behind it is still in progress. Measure and Analyse are complete and point at tool wear, but Improve and Control are not signed, so line 3 cannot be re-qualified for commercial output. For scale: PPQ produces 3 batches as the norm, so 3 affected commercial batches is a full run's worth of the launch quantity.

evidence.label: Where
evidence.value: Line 3 — 3 commercial batches out of spec; line 5 unaffected

evidence.label: Why not fixed yet
evidence.value: CAPA overdue — DMAIC Improve/Control still in progress

evidence.label: Scale
evidence.value: PPQ norm is 3 batches (a validation run was 12 at one site), so this is a full run's worth of commercial volume

evidence.label: Gate
evidence.value: G3 holds on all three routes — this is a volume call, not a schedule one

evidence.label: Routes
evidence.value: Re-prioritise markets · drive the DMAIC to close · move to another qualified site (same modality)

answer.rec: Re-prioritise markets and redistribute the reduced commercial volume
why: Fewer commercial batches means the launch quantity has to be reallocated — protect the lead markets, defer the lower-priority ones
Closing the CAPA via the in-progress DMAIC recovers line 3, but only once Improve and Control sign off
Moving to another same-modality site is viable only if the agents confirm regulatory/engineering clearance AND open capacity
answer.confidence: High confidence · read from the line MES, the SPC record and the open CAPA/DMAIC.

question: The FDA slipped Berobenatide OA's clearance six weeks — what moves?
subtitle: One authority date, five downstream commitments, two calls that are yours

prose: The FDA moved Berobenatide OA's NDA clearance from 02 Nov to 14 Dec — a six-week slip on a date you don't control. Manufacturing has already built launch stock, the launch stock are staged at the 3PL, and the field is trained for the original go-live. The old way, that slip becomes a ten-week scramble across three teams. Here it cascades in one pass: three commitments re-time themselves, and exactly two need a human.

evidence.label: Manufacturing · auto-adjusted
evidence.value: Production Run 2 (launch-stock top-up) held to the new clearance date. No second run committed against a date the agency has already moved.

evidence.label: Logistics · auto-adjusted
evidence.value: Launch stock deployment across the US geographies re-timed to the new go-live. The 3PL is not asked to ship against the old date.

evidence.label: Commercial · auto-adjusted
evidence.value: KOL pre-announcement accounts flagged for proactive outreach, so the field is not selling a date the FDA just moved.

evidence.label: Finance · needs you
evidence.value: Six extra weeks of finished-goods storage. Extend the 3PL slot (+€48k carrying cost, zero re-stage risk) or repatriate to the regional DC (saves €36k, adds a 9-day re-stage). J. Ruiz owns it.

evidence.label: Field readiness · needs you
evidence.value: Certification currency drifts past the new go-live. Recertify now, or schedule a single refresh two weeks out. T. Bergmann owns it.

answer.rec: Take the two human calls in one sitting; the other three are already re-planned
why: The three auto-adjusted commitments have a known rule — move with the clearance date — so the platform re-timed them and recorded it, rather than asking
The two that reach you are genuine trade-offs (carrying cost vs re-stage risk; recertify-now vs single-refresh) that no rule can settle
Leadership sees the €48k working-capital impact the moment the date moves, not three days later
answer.confidence: Read from the connected-milestone graph — every downstream commitment carries its own re-plan rule and owner, so the split into auto vs human is derived, not typed.
